headline: OpenAI Foundation Commits $250 Million to Help Workers Navigate AI-Driven Job Displacement
raw_snippet: The OpenAI Foundation, which holds a 26% stake in OpenAI's for-profit business, announced on May 27 it will commit at least $250 million toward grants, research partnerships, and direct programs to help workers and economies adapt to AI-driven disruption. The funds will back labor market research, support workers facing near-term displacement, and explore new mechanisms for distributing AI-generated wealth more broadly. This is the Foundation's first major initiative; first programs expected before end of 2026.

headline: Sam Altman Says AI Will Not Lead to 'Jobs Apocalypse,' Admits Previous Predictions Were Wrong
raw_snippet: Speaking at a Commonwealth Bank of Australia conference in Sydney on May 26, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the AI boom will not cause a 'jobs apocalypse,' admitting he was 'pretty wrong' about AI's social and economic impact. He said he expected more disruption to entry-level white-collar jobs by now and was 'delighted to be wrong.' The remarks were widely covered by Reuters, Bloomberg, and Time. The comments came days after OpenAI filed its confidential S-1.

headline: Anthropic Eclipses OpenAI's Valuation with $965 Billion Series H Funding Round
raw_snippet: Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H round valuing the company at $965 billion, surpassing OpenAI's $852 billion valuation from March for the first time. The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital. Anthropic's run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion, up from ~$14 billion at its February Series G. This intensifies the competitive battle as both companies approach potential IPOs.

headline: OpenAI Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise AI Coding Agents
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on May 27 that it was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise AI Coding Agents. Gartner recognized Codex's strengths across agentic software development, enterprise governance, sandboxing, and flexible deployment options. Codex is now used by more than 4 million developers weekly, with companies including NVIDIA among enterprise customers.

headline: OpenAI Publishes Frontier Governance Framework Aligning with California and EU AI Regulations
raw_snippet: OpenAI published its Frontier Governance Framework on May 29, a public document explaining how its safety and security practices align with California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act (TFAIA) and the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General Purpose AI. The framework covers risk assessment across cyber offense, CBRN risks, harmful manipulation, and loss of control scenarios, as well as model reporting, security risk management, incident response, and external expert input.

headline: OpenAI Launches Rosalind Biodefense Program, Offering Free GPT-Rosalind Access for Pandemic Preparedness
raw_snippet: OpenAI launched Rosalind Biodefense on May 29, expanding trusted access to its specialized life sciences model GPT-Rosalind for vetted developers, U.S. government agencies, academic institutions, and nonprofit developers working on pandemic preparedness and biodefense. OpenAI covers API costs for vetted partners. Axios reported the launch as an exclusive. The program supports epidemiological modeling, early detection, screening, and preparedness work.

headline: OpenAI Releases Shared Playbook for Trustworthy Third-Party Evaluations of Frontier Models
raw_snippet: OpenAI published guidance on May 29 addressing what makes for effective independent evaluations of frontier AI model safeguards and capabilities. The playbook covers how evaluation harnesses, claims, and resource budgets affect measurement reliability, and recommends approaches for valid assessment as models gain tool-use, multi-step reasoning, and error-recovery capabilities. This complements the Frontier Governance Framework published the same day.

headline: OpenAI and Thrive Holdings Showcase Self-Improving AI Tax Agent Built with Codex, Achieving 97% Accuracy
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a case study on May 27 showing how its forward deployed engineers and Thrive Holdings built a self-improving AI tax system using Codex that achieved up to 97% accuracy. The system processed 7,000 tax returns in a pilot across Crete Professional Alliance's 30+ accounting firms, cutting preparation time by a third and boosting throughput by 50%. OpenAI acquired an equity stake in Thrive Holdings in December 2025.

headline: OpenAI Publishes 2026 Election Safeguards Plan Ahead of Midterm Elections
raw_snippet: OpenAI outlined election information safeguards for 2026 on May 27, partnering with the Associated Press for live vote counts and Democracy Works for voter registration info. The company is offering Codex Security to voting system manufacturers, briefing election officials on AI cyber capabilities, investing in content provenance with SynthID watermarks, and endorsing the Protect Elections From Deceptive AI Act and the Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act.

headline: OpenAI Updates GPT-5.5 Instant with Improved Response Style, Retires Canvas from GPT-5.5 Models
raw_snippet: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API on May 28 to improve response style and quality, making responses easier to read, more natural in everyday conversations, and better paced. Canvas is no longer available in GPT-5.5 Instant or GPT-5.5 Thinking; writing and coding functionality is now handled through in-chat writing blocks and code blocks, which OpenAI says halve latency for code execution versus Canvas sessions.

headline: OpenAI Announces Retirement of o3 (August 26) and GPT-4.5 (June 27) from ChatGPT
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced around May 28 that o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset period. Both models remain available to paid users via model settings during the sunset window and through the API indefinitely. The retirements continue OpenAI's consolidation onto GPT-5.5 as the primary model.

headline: OpenAI Brings Codex Computer Use to Windows, Adds Mobile Remote Control
raw_snippet: OpenAI released Codex app version 26.527 on May 29, bringing Computer Use to Windows. Codex can now see, click, and type in Windows desktop apps. Users can remotely start or steer Codex on a Windows machine from ChatGPT on iOS, Android, or Mac. The update also added Codex Profiles with usage stats and token activity tracking. Previously, Computer Use was available only on Mac.

headline: Codex CLI v0.134.0 Released with Conversation History Search, Profile Overhaul, and MCP OAuth
raw_snippet: Codex CLI v0.134.0 was released on May 26 with searchable local conversation history (case-insensitive with result previews), --profile as the canonical selector replacing legacy configs, per-server MCP environment targeting with OAuth for streamable HTTP, improved schema reliability for connector tools, concurrent read-only MCP tool execution, and enhanced Windows install robustness removing VC++ runtime DLL dependency.

headline: OpenAI, Grupo Folha, and Grupo UOL Announce Strategic Content Partnership for Brazilian Market
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced its first media partnership in Brazil on May 25, bringing Folha de S.Paulo and UOL journalism to ChatGPT's 900+ million weekly active users. Grupo Folha and Grupo UOL gain access to Codex, ChatGPT Enterprise, and API for journalism workflows. Brazil is one of ChatGPT's largest markets with over 50 million monthly active users and ~140 million messages per day.

headline: Florida Attorney General Files First-Ever State Lawsuit Against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman Over Product Safety
raw_snippet: Florida AG James Uthmeier filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman personally on May 31, accusing the company of prioritizing profits over safety. The suit alleges deceptive trade practices, negligence, product liability, fraudulent misrepresentation, and public nuisance, stemming from the April 2025 FSU mass shooting where the perpetrator had ~16,000 ChatGPT interactions. This is the first time a U.S. state has sued OpenAI and its leadership personally over product design and safety.

headline: Illinois Legislature Passes Landmark AI Safety Bill Requiring Third-Party Audits; OpenAI Supports
raw_snippet: The Illinois House unanimously passed SB 315 (110-0) on May 27, requiring frontier AI companies to publish safety plans and undergo annual independent third-party audits — a first for U.S. AI legislation. OpenAI and Anthropic publicly supported the bill. Governor Pritzker plans to sign it into law. The bill includes whistleblower protections for AI company employees and mirrors California and New York provisions on safety disclosures.

headline: Bloomberg Reports OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic IPOs Could Fuel $70B in Additional AI Supply Chain Spending
raw_snippet: Bloomberg reported on May 31 that the upcoming IPOs of SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic may trigger up to $70 billion in additional AI infrastructure spending on top of $750B+ already committed by hyperscalers. Investors are increasingly betting on Asian supply chain beneficiaries including Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Ibiden, Hon Hai Precision, Quanta Computer, and MediaTek.

headline: OpenAI Files Confidential S-1 IPO Prospectus with SEC, Targeting $852B-$1T Valuation for September
raw_snippet: OpenAI filed a confidential S-1 IPO prospectus with the SEC on May 22, targeting a Q4 2026 public listing at a valuation between $852 billion and $1 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the deal. The S-1 stays sealed until ~15 days before the public roadshow. Fortune, CNBC, Reuters, Axios, and Bloomberg all confirmed the filing. This could be one of the largest technology IPOs in history.

headline: OpenAI's Q1 2026 Revenue Reported at $5.7 Billion Despite -122% Operating Margin
raw_snippet: Reports published May 22 showed OpenAI generated ~$5.7 billion in Q1 2026 revenue (~$2B per month run rate), driven by ChatGPT subscriptions, Codex enterprise adoption, and early ad revenue. The company posted a -122% adjusted operating margin, losing $1.22 for every $1 of revenue. OpenAI leads rival Anthropic by ~$1 billion in quarterly revenue, though Anthropic is growing faster and expects to more than double Q1 revenue in Q2.

headline: Elon Musk Loses Lawsuit Against OpenAI on Statute of Limitations, Vows Appeal to Ninth Circuit
raw_snippet: A jury in Oakland, California, unanimously ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI on May 18, finding the case was filed outside a three-year statute of limitations. The court did not rule on the merits of Musk's breach of charitable trust claims. Musk called the verdict a 'calendar technicality' and vowed to appeal to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. The judge expressed skepticism about the appeal.

headline: OpenAI Responds to TanStack npm Supply Chain Attack, Two Employee Devices Compromised, macOS Certificate Revocation Set for June 12
raw_snippet: OpenAI disclosed that two employee devices were compromised in the TanStack npm supply chain attack (Mini Shai-Hulud) on May 11. Attackers accessed a limited subset of internal source code repositories and code-signing certificates. No user data or products were compromised. OpenAI is revoking its macOS app signing certificate on June 12, requiring all macOS users to update ChatGPT Desktop, Codex App, Codex CLI, and Atlas. TechCrunch, The Register, and SecurityWeek covered the incident extensively.

headline: OpenAI Model Disproves 80-Year-Old Erdős Unit Distance Conjecture in Discrete Geometry
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced on May 20 that an internal reasoning model independently disproved the Erdős unit distance conjecture, a central problem in discrete geometry from 1946. The model found a new family of constructions that beat the grid arrangement and proved it mathematically. This is the first time AI has autonomously solved a prominent open problem central to a field of mathematics. The result was also published on arXiv.

headline: Greg Brockman Reveals Details of 72-Hour Crisis After Sam Altman's 2023 Firing in First Public Podcast
raw_snippet: OpenAI President Greg Brockman appeared on the Knowledge Project podcast, recounting in detail for the first time the 72 hours after Sam Altman was fired in November 2023. Brockman described the board call, his same-day resignation, the 'Phoenix' backup company designed at Altman's house, and the moment Ilya Sutskever's tweet changed everything. He also discussed how much of OpenAI's code is now AI-written and the company's views on the AI race.
